observation.visible_scene: A close view of a blue-felt pool table. A person in a red shirt stands at the far rail holding a wooden cue stick aimed at a white cue ball marked with red dots. A red-and-white striped 15-ball sits between the cue ball and the camera. An out-of-focus orange ball occupies the lower-left foreground early on.
visible_changes: The cue tip is drawn to and contacts the white cue ball, then pulls back as the cue ball begins rolling forward (toward the camera) away from the stick.
The rolling white cue ball closes the gap to the striped 15-ball and makes contact with it around the middle of the segment.
After contact, both balls travel toward the camera, growing larger in frame; the striped 15-ball leads while the white cue ball trails, gradually shifting to the 15-ball's right side.

Both balls rotate visibly (the '15' on the striped ball turns upright and back, the red dots on the cue ball spin), and their forward motion slows until they are nearly stationary, the 15-ball on the left and the cue ball on the right.
The player's red-shirted torso and the cue stick recede out of the top of the frame as the segment progresses.
The blurred orange foreground ball, present in the lower-left for the first half, leaves the frame in the later half.
outside_clip_unknowns: The intended shot line, the player's aim, and any result of the shot after the excerpt ends.
What happened before t=0 (the cue was already being drawn back at the first frame).
Whether the foreground orange ball was struck or simply moved out of view.
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the background player and the top rail leaving the frame is due to camera tilt/zoom or to the player stepping back; the balls' apparent growth is consistent with them rolling toward a fixed camera, but some camera movement cannot be ruled out.
The exact moment of cue-ball/15-ball contact is inferred from their closing then shared motion, not seen as a sharp impact.
The disappearance of the foreground orange ball is a framing/focus change, not a visible removal of the object.
